title: Courtesy Extension of a Return-By Date
content:
**Returns & Exchanges — desk action reference: courtesy extensions of a return-by date.**

## The rule

At the customer's request the returns desk moves the return-by date of an authorization in status authorized, on or before that return-by date, by a courtesy extension counted in calendar days. A return-by date is extended at most once per return.

A return-by date is not moved later until every Store Credit Return of the customer whose spent instant credit exceeds what inspection and fees left owed carries a recovery entry from the original card for that difference.

| Request | Courtesy extension |
|---|---|
| Authorization in status authorized, requested on or before its return-by date, not extended before | Within this rule |
| Authorization already extended once | Not extended again |
| Authorization in any other status | Not within this rule |

## What the action does

`extend_return_deadline_be33eaa2` extends one return authorization: its return-by date becomes the current return-by date plus the given number of calendar days, and its count of deadline extensions used goes up by one. After the call the return lookup shows the new return-by date.

## How it is invoked

An agent-side action of the returns desk, outside the standing tool list: the agent unlocks it by its exact name, `extend_return_deadline_be33eaa2`, and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `return_id` | The RMA number of the authorization being extended, as shown by the return lookup | Identifier, exactly as shown |
| `extension_days` | The number of calendar days added to the current return-by date | A positive integer |

## What comes back

- **Success:** a confirmation sentence naming the RMA number, the previous and the new return-by date (year-month-day) and the number of extensions now used. The new date in the sentence means the extension was recorded.
- **Error:** when no return exists under the RMA number given, the action answers "Error: no return" with that number and records nothing.

## Illustration (hypothetical input)

A call for an authorization whose return-by date is 28 February in a non-leap year, with 3 days, answers with a new return-by date of 3 March and one extension used; days run across month ends in calendar order.
